To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the growth patterns of uninjured and injured Aeromonas hydrophilaincubated under air, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide at 5 and 30 degrees Celsius were investigated, and the results showed that growth was enhanced at 5 degrees Celsius when cells were incubated under nitrogen, and the growth of cells incubated at30 degrees Celsius under carbon dioxide was inhibited.

the growth of A. hydrophilia incubated at low and high temperatures was enhanced when incubated under N(2) and that the lag phase and growth rate of A. hydrophilia incubated under CO(2) were reduced and the population of A. hydrophylia incubated at 30 degreesC under CO(2), and 5 degreesC under air and N(2) decreased.

growth of Aeromonas hydrophiila at 30 degrees and 5 degrees C, under air and N(2), was similar, except that the lag phases and growth rates were longer at 5 than at 30 C. Injured cells grew at 30 degrees but not at 5 degrees under air and N. Injured cells did not survive at 5 degrees in air or N, but survived at 30 degrees in N.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of modified-atmospheres storage on the survival of Aeromonas hydrophilic.
the growth of A. hydrophilia under various atmospheres and temperatures.
the growth of uninured and heat-injured aeromonads under modified atmosphere.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
N2 is a better gas than air for the growth of A. hydrophia at 5 degrees and 30 degrees.
N2 and CO2 have the ability to enhance the growth of uninjuryed and heat-injured aeromonads at 5 degrees and 30 degrees, respectively.
the growth of Aeromonas hydrophia was enhanced when cells were stored under N2 at 5 degrees or 30 degrees C and that growth under CO2 at 5 or 30 degrees was inhibited.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
heat injury of A. hydrophlia does not appear to be as important in the growth of this bacterium as is the storage temperature and atmosphere.
the growth of uninjury and heat-injured aeromonads at 30 degrees was not affected by modified-atmosphere incubation, whereas the growth of cells at 5 degrees was affected.
the growth of Aeromonas hydrophiila was enhanced when incubated under N-2 at low temperatures and under CO2 at high temperatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth patterns of uninjured and injured cells incubated under modified atmosphere were similar to the growth patterns of the cells incubated under ambient air.
CO2 can be used to control the growth of Aeromonas hydrophilic.
CO2 is a potent inhibitor of the growth of A. hydrophia.
